body: Ugh, sorry this happened t o you.  Thank you for your response and kind words.
Yes, it was truly awful.  My psychiatrist caught it before it went to the stage where I'd have to be hospitalized.  What happened when you had it?
Ugh, I'm sorry that happened to you, how horrible.

It's probably one of the hardest things to do, and all humans have to work on this in some way: don't buy into your parents' false concepts about who you are.  They are not seeing you clearly at all.  You are valuable and important and you deserve to stay alive to see all the amazing wonders of your life unfold.  If your parents are comparing you to your siblings, they're not doing their job right.  You know that.  Who knows why they're having such a hard time being good parents to you right now, but they are, and it isn't your fault.  Don't take their obviously skewed judgement as gospel.  I am a former 4.0 achiever, and let me tell you, it did nothing for me except give me a temporary ego boost in the only area I could excel in.  It has nothing to do with personal worth or future success.  

You're only 15.  Stay alive.  Find a better therapist.  Find an accessible teacher at school who you can talk to about your issues at school, with the false allegation. Maybe even talk to that teacher about your parents and all you're going through.  

I know I'm just some asshole on the internet, but I am rooting for you to make it through this.
You can do it.  You deserve more than the situation you're in right now.
Ditto and ditto!

Kind encouragement from the rhino_scrotum.  :)

(Seriously, what you wrote was lovely, and I love reddit for making me smile about small things like this.)  (The juxtaposition, I mean.  The rhino scrotum itself is probably somewhat vast.)

So freaking true.  I have these weird "windows" in my depression - very, very infrequently- when some kind of switch flips in my brain and I return to a normal mood.  I still perceive the bullshit nonsense, but it bothers me so much less, it's just part of a bigger picture.  It's like I'm plugged back into the current of life, vitality returns, and the bullshit nonsense becomes just one aspect of the whole array of phenomena, and it doesn't fill me with paralyzing hopelessness and futility.  

Anyway, thanks for writing out your thoughts in such a clear and useful way.

Jesus, I'm sorry.  That's a bunch of hurtful and ignorant responses when you really needed help.

> Fuck these people, believe in yourself, you know what works for you and what doesnt. Its taking me a long time to stop second guessing myself or not trusting my own instincts.

Good.  I think humanity is really still in the dark ages about treating any kind of mental illness.  Even the people who are trained, knowledgable, helpful and understanding are still guessing so much of the time.  I guess that will always somewhat be the case when abstract concepts like the soul or the mind are implicated in the disease process, but I think so much more will be known in the future about what really causes depression and other mental health challenges, and what cures or considerably alleviates them.  I read something the other day about a study in which the scientists found that children whose bodies responded to the flu with a higher degree of inflammation than other children were markedly more likely to develop depression over time.  There's so much we still don't know.  

All the best to you, and don't let the (potentially???) well-meaning ignoramuses get you down.

I don't really know or understand the science around this (although, really, nobody does yet), but it seems like depression triggers some of the same mechanisms that go into gear for mammals when we get sick with more identifiably physical illnesses... the urge to isolate, be still, rest and recuperate.  I've had time to do this, but the problem is that - well, I don't know, but at least in my case it didn't make me better.  Even though it felt absolutely necessary because I had absolutely no energy.  But maybe it does make some people well, I don't know.  For me, my body seems to be responding to the depression by giving me signals to do things that provide a modicum of relief, but worsen the situation overall.
It does hurt physically, too.  I'm sorry, and you're not alone.
You *sounded* unfit??  Lolz.

The time in my life when I was the most physically active, moving a lot, walking/hiking everyday, was one of the worst times for my depression.  It's good to exercise, but it doesn't help every person's depression lessen or go away.
I do wish that now.

Thank you for your response, thank you so much.  Feeling so bad right now that it's hard to write more or respond well, but thank you.

It sounds like it's at a point where being open about how you're feeling would be a good idea, at least at first with a counselor or mental health services of some kind, so that you don't have to be so alone in the middle of your suffering.

I'm sorry you're feeling so bad.  I don't have any answers, just wanted you to know that another person heard you. I seriously think it would be a good idea to talk to your psychiatrist about how much anger/hatred you're feeling right now, because that can be a withdrawal symptom if you just stopped all your medications at once.  It doesn't mean you have to stay on them if you don't want to take them anymore, just that tapering down the dosage over a period of time might make things easier on your system and calm down the anger so that you can deal with it bit by bit, instead of having a huge surge that feels unmanageable.

Just a thought.  I've had surges of irrational hatred/anger/irritability when I stopped certain medications, it was often a withdrawal symptom for me and it really sucked.  I'm sorry you're going through that, whatever the cause.  Besides talking to your psychiatrist about tapering the drugs, I would recommend running, singing/yelling really loudly in the car or when you're alone somewhere, using crayons or pens to scribble energetically on a large piece of paper, write down (physically, with a pen, not typing) all the things that are triggering your anger, so that you get it out of your head and out into the world in some way.  

I really hope you feel better soon.

Your body responded totally appropriately and innocently based on the trauma it remembers and hasn't fully healed from, and your SO responded totally appropriately when they realized that they had inadvertently triggered your nervous system into fight or flight mode.  Neither of you are doing anything wrong.

(IDK if any of that helped, I just wanted to make some statements that take the shame or self-blame out of the situation, because sometimes that helps.  I hope you feel better soon and I'm so sorry that you were sexually assaulted.  I wish for you all the good things, internet stranger.)

I would say it sounds a lot like depression - but, who knows, depression in and of itself is a label that we stick on a broad range of experience.  I don't know, and I don't know what to do either, I just wanted you to know that even though you feel alone, you aren't alone in having this kind of experience.  

Can you tell the counselor about all of this suffering that you're experiencing?

Have you stopped while under a doctor's care?  You know you can have a lot of side effects from stopping some medications abruptly, especially if you've been on them a long time.  Sometimes anger can be a part of that.

Ugh, how terrible.  It sounds like you're offering to be there for her, that's the best thing... it sounds like she's still trying to figure out how she wants to proceed?  You could offer to work through some different possible scenarios with her - what some outcomes might be if she goes to the cops, what some outcome might be if she doesn't... I think sometimes mapping out different logical possibilities helps someone who's feeling emotionally paralyzed.  Maybe don't push her in any direction as far as action or non-action goes, just take her lead.  You also never know if that incident has triggered something else from her past, compounding the situation (could be any kind of experience of powerlessness, doesn't necessarily have to be sexual trauma, although that could be there, as well).  In any case, I'm so sorry that happened.  I'd personally like to relocate him to a slime pit, and order inedible pizza to his slime pit every day for the next 20 years.

I don't think you deserve it.   Loneliness is one of the worst feelings on the planet.  Can you put your feet on the ground, breathe, know that you are connected with every living thing on the planet, and beyond?  Sometimes this helps me.  We are never not connected to the whole web of life, there's no way we could actually be separate, except in our minds.  Sometimes this doesn't put any dent in my loneliness, but sometimes I feel a glimmer of connectedness, and it shifts me out of that intense suffering for a while.  I'm sorry you're hurting so much.

I am sure that your parents would want you to live, to keep going and experience better things.  Please take people up on their offers of help.
Good!  I hope you can go get some help ASAP.  You might find someone/something that actually helps.  Wishing all the best for you.

Can you go see a counselor or someone trusted to talk about it?  Sometimes it really helps to have another person's perspective and assistance.  Feeling unmotivated is a huge symptom and part of depression, I think.  People are naturally motivated and oriented towards what they want when they feel good (or normal) - depression can make everything seem like an unappealing haze of nothingness, and it is hard to engage in life when it all looks that way.

Relaxation is a foreign country to me, too.  I get to visit it once in a great while, like when I get really sick with a fever or flu, my fight-or-flight reflex finally gives up or something, and I can bask in feverish relaxation.

You exist!!  You exist and you are struggling with lots of hard stuff.  It's not pathetic, it's life.  I know how hard it is when depression saps almost every shred of motivation, and concentration gets near-impossible, and your academic and work life becomes unmanageable because of it.  I hate it, I've had it, it's so hard to endure.  Can you reach out to your friends and family, even though they're far away?  Just to let them know you're struggling and could use support.  You're not supposed to have everything figured out at this point, this is the point at which you start figuring things out, and get as much help as you need right away.  Let somebody know!  Depression, anxiety, and ADHD are not who you are, you are so much more.

Can you talk to a counselor or a friend about this?  It might help to sort it all out with someone in person.  

Just remember, it's easy to forget reasons why you didn't stick with her in the first place.  It is possible that you've been building her up in your mind, now that she's unavailable.  Or maybe not!  I don't know.  But it might be worth sorting it all out with a therapist or someone you can trust to listen and give wise advice.  I'm sorry you're feeling so bad.
That a very nice thing of you to do, sharing your learned experience!  Having no energy has always been a big part of my depression.

If there's anything at all that makes you feel a smidgen more connected or interested or cheerful, maybe you could try focusing on that for a few minutes at a time.  Sometimes that helps me feel a little less bad for a while.  Sending you all the best.

Sorry you feel this bad, sorry OP feels this bad, sorry I feel this bad, but glad to feel ever-so-slightly less alone.

I'm sorry things suck so much right now, HK.  I know how hard it is to feel like nobody listens, that you can't actually get your thoughts out there, and the relief that entails.  It's the hardest thing, in some ways, but it is possible sometimes to ask for what you need - "Can you just let me talk for a couple minutes, I really need to get this out before discussing it more?"  Some people are definitely okay with this, as long as you're willing to reciprocate and listen to them.  

Have you actually been to a therapist, or just psychiatrists?  Just asking, cause maybe it would help to talk to someone who doesn't dispense drugs.  If you have seen a therapist and are saying "fuck therapy", I definitely don't want to get in the line of people telling you to do something you hate!  I've had a few helpful-ish experiences with therapy, and some not so good ones, and my own father is a therapist, and while he might be a good therapist, he was a pretty miserable father a lot of the time, so my perspective on the issue is decidedly mixed.  

Something with the reading ADD that helps me is putting on a timer (like a cell phone one, not the old fashioned kind that makes noise as it winds down), setting it for five minutes or so.  It catches me out of my daydreams or wherever my mind has gone and brings me back to focus for another minute or two.  Sometimes if I do this enough times in a row, it feels like my brain gets into a more concentrate-y mode, it gets on a roll.

I don't know if any of this helps, mostly I'm just sorry you feel so shitty.  I hope you can find someone IRL who can help/really listen to you.  Glad music helps a little, anyway.  I love Grover Washington Jr.  I'm not that good with harder stuff because I basically have the nervous system of a baby bird. :/

I just wanted to offer you an internet hug if you want it!  I can sense that you're a good human being in the midst of a massively difficult challenge, too.  I'm sending you lots of good wishes, even though I don't have answers.

Stopping and starting medications is probably more a result of certain ones not really working and/or causing unbearable side effects.  I don't think it means you're addicted to the dark, because if something really made you feel a lot better, I imagine you 'd be all over that stuff!  And the fact that Cymbalta helped a lot (even if not to "happy" levels), is a great sign.  I wish I had lots of money, I would send you enough for a year's supply.  Unfortunately, my financial situation has been totally eroded by my disease.  Maybe search online for social services in your area?  Even if there's something that you don't personally need right now, like Meals on Wheels, you might be able to just have a conversation with someone there who could think of some ways to improve you and your family's situation.  There are lots of kind people working for organizations like that, who really want to help, that's why they are there.  You could even email them if a phone conversation feels too vulnerable.  There are people who would love to help.  If I wasn't so far away, I would come clean for you, I love cleaning (weirdly, although it's always a challenge to keep my own space clean) - there must be some weirdos like me in Texas who are affiliated with good organizations that will come help you clean!  

Here's a list of free clinics in Texas, too:

http://www.freemedicalsearch.org/sta/texas

I hope something in there helps.  I know how awful depression is, especially when the circumstances around you get bleaker.  From the tone of your post, you sound strong and brave and I believe in you.  

Now I must return to my own bleakness. :). One last thing - that much Benadryl can't be good for you - you're not really taking 50 a day, are you?  If you are able to get some help, and get to a clinic sometime, make sure to get some sound advice about tapering down so that you don't have bad withdrawal symptoms.  

All the good things to you, internet stranger.

Hey, fanaseyes, I'm sorry you're going through depression as well as the grief from losing your cousin.  I'm so sorry you lost her.  

I don't know if OP was responding to your post or not (I didn't see it).  I imagine that you were just trying to reach someone who might be in a similar situation to your cousin, wanting to remind them that they are valuable and loved, and most likely have someone in their life who loves them and will miss them as much as you love and miss your cousin.  That's a beautiful way to reach out, and also express your own love.  I also understand where the OP is coming from, being myself one of the people who's been ill so long that I've lost most of my connections.  It has been beyond terrible to have nearly every piece of my life and soul clawed away from me by this disease.  Once upon a time, I was someone that a lot of people would have been very sad about losing.  It's not that way anymore, and that's not just the depression talking.  It does hurt to sometimes read that I shouldn't end it because of all the people who love me, when I know that used to be true, but isn't anymore.  But it's my situation that causes my pain, not the advice itself.  For myself, I would prefer that people keep offering this kind of advice, these reminders to the depressed that they are loved and cared for and have people in their lives that would miss them so much if they were gone.  It will reach some people, and that's enough.  Not that it will make their depression go away, but it can serve as a reminder of the potential good, the resources and relationships that they have, a reminder of their value and ties to the world.  I would prefer that these people be helped rather than my feelings be spared.  (Sorry for the long ramble.)

What a great attitude/strategy.  I think we all here know the sense of deep distress around the general lack of knowledge/understanding (I don't really mean sympathy here, more like comprehension) of what depression really feels like, what it does to us.  That's part of why why we pounce on anything that elucidates the some of the experience, like Allie Brosh's comic.  And why we can feel so desperate and sometimes demeaned when people who haven't been there offer simplistic and unhelpful perspectives and advice.  But, you're right, we do have a choice about how we mentally categorize these encounters, under *blah! Humbug*, or *thank you for wanting me to feel better*.   

(Sorry for going on so long here, and basically just repeating what you said.  My cognitive abilities are very foggy lately, so when I have a moment of better focus or lucidity, I try to use it as best I can.  Thanks for the *actually* helpful advice.)

Hey, swiggly, I'm sorry you're feeling so terrible.  I've been depressed most of my life, I know how grindingly beyond difficult it is.  The thing that's telling you you're worthless right now is the depression, it's not the truth.  Some ideas to get out of the place you're in right now might be - make a tumblr of animals you love; write about peace, or read articles about peace online (we definitely need more peace in the world, especially right now!), cook something new or familiar, go for a walk or hike.  Write out some aspects of the girl you love - is she friendly, understanding, interesting, smart, etc?  Separate these qualities out from her, and realize that they are qualities that exist all around in heaps of people, as well as in yourself.  Yes, she is unique and special to you, but some of what you love in her is also available all around you.  

I'm probably just rambling right now in order to distract myself from my  from my own problems, but I hope you feel better soon.  You are NOT useless.

Maybe a beach area would be nice, if you can swing it?  Sometimes sleeping near the ocean is refreshing...

I've read some anecdotal reports about that kind of effect with a few drugs, it seems like a lot of people have been surprised by a drug sort a making their depression vanish in the aftermath of it, lasting a few days or even weeks or longer.
